q-4064.name: Question 1
q-4064.worked_solution:
We simplify each of the radical terms using the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{27}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-\sqrt{{x}^{5}} & = \\ 3\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{9\cdot 3}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-\sqrt{{x}^{4}\cdot x} & = \\ 3\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{9}\cdot \sqrt{3}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-\sqrt{{x}^{4}}\cdot \sqrt{x} & = \\ 3\sqrt{3}-3\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2}\sqrt{x} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we combine the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{3}-3\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2}\sqrt{x} & = \\ (3-3)\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2}\sqrt{x} & = \\ 0\cdot \sqrt{3}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2}\sqrt{x} & = \\ 3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2}\sqrt{x} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-4064.html:
Question 1
?

33−27+3x23−x5=

a
3+3x23−x2x
b
3x2−x53
c
x23−3xx
d
3x23−x2x
e
3+3x23−xx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We simplify each of the radical terms using the product rule: 33−27+3x23−x5=33−9⋅3+3x23−x4⋅x=33−9⋅3+3x23−x4⋅x=33−33+3x23−x2x

Finally, we combine the like terms: 33−33+3x23−x2x=(3−3)3+3x23−x2x=0⋅3+3x23−x2x=3x23−x2x

q-29319.name: Question 2
q-29319.worked_solution:
We can combine the two $\sqrt[3]{y}$ terms together, and the two $\sqrt{y}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\sqrt[3]{y}-4\sqrt{y}-7\sqrt[3]{y}+2\sqrt{y} & = \\ (-4+2)\sqrt{y}+(3-7)\sqrt[3]{y} & = \\ -2\sqrt{y}-4\sqrt[3]{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we cannot combine the $\sqrt[3]{y}$ and $\sqrt{y}$ terms.

q-29319.html:
Question 2
?

Simplify 3y3−4y−7y3+2y.

a
4y−2y3
b
2y−4y3
c
−2y−4y3
d
−y−5y3
e
−6y
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can combine the two y3 terms together, and the two y terms together:

3y3−4y−7y3+2y=(−4+2)y+(3−7)y3=−2y−4y3

Notice that we cannot combine the y3 and y terms.

q-29322.name: Question 3
q-29322.worked_solution:
We simplify each of the radical terms using the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\sqrt{54}+2x\sqrt{x}-5x\sqrt{6} & = \\ 2x\sqrt{9\cdot 6}+2x\sqrt{x}-5x\sqrt{6} & = \\ 2x\sqrt{9}\cdot \sqrt{6}+2x\sqrt{x}-5x\sqrt{6} & = \\ 2x\cdot 3\cdot \sqrt{6}+2x\sqrt{x}-5x\sqrt{6} & = \\ 6x\sqrt{6}+2x\sqrt{x}-5x\sqrt{6} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we combine the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x\sqrt{6}+2x\sqrt{x}-5x\sqrt{6} & = \\ (6x-5x)\sqrt{6}+2x\sqrt{x} & = \\ x\sqrt{6}+2x\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

q-29322.html:
Question 3
?

Simplify 2x54+2xx−5x6.

a
6+x
b
x6+2xx
c
x6
d
x6−xx
e
x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We simplify each of the radical terms using the product rule: 2x54+2xx−5x6=2x9⋅6+2xx−5x6=2x9⋅6+2xx−5x6=2x⋅3⋅6+2xx−5x6=6x6+2xx−5x6 Finally, we combine the like terms: 6x6+2xx−5x6=(6x−5x)6+2xx=x6+2xx
